newsitem.title: MEXICO: Pemex says 10-mos crude exports draw $8.754 bln.
newsitem.headline: Pemex says 10-mos crude exports draw $8.754 bln.

text.p: Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex) said it earned $8.754 billion from crude exports in the first 10 months of the year, Mexico's state-owned oil and gas monopoly said in a statement Wednesday.
Income from such exports rose by $2.505 billion over the same period in 1995 as oil prices reached post-Gulf War highs.
Crude oil exports averaged 1.55 million barrels per day (bpd), the company said.
Pemex said it exported 190,300 bpd of light crude Isthmus, which generated $1.134 billion in the first 10 months of the year. The average price of each barrel was $19.54 per barrel.
Foreign sales of an average 874,100 bpd heavy Maya crude drew income of $4.505 billion from January to October, the company said. A barrel of Maya was sold at an average price of $16.90.
Extra-light Olmeca crude sales, averaging 487,800 bpd with average barrel prices at $20.94, totalled $3.115 billion in the time period, Pemex said.

Of Pemex's crude exports, 78 percent was sold to the United States, 7.8 percent to other destinations in the Americas, 6.4 percent to Spain, 1.8 percent to other European coutries and six percent to the Far East.
